claims.text: Same per-task resolution guard as Tier 1/arms: a bad repo label or an unindexed target must not take down an opt-in, potentially long-running LLM run over the rest of the task set.
claims.why: The comment describes intent; the code catches ValueError and OSError, but the guard's presence and adequacy cannot be fully verified without seeing Tier 1 implementation and the definitions of resolve_task_repo, cached_index, _whole_repo_text.

claims.text: Read baseline.json, or an empty baseline if it does not exist yet (a fresh repo checkout before the first ``--update-baseline`` run).
claims.why: The function checks os.path.exists(p) and returns {'schema': 1, 'tasks': {}} if not exists; otherwise reads and returns json.load.

claims.text: Pure: build the baseline structure for the CURRENT recall of ``tasks`` (default TASKS). Does not touch disk -- see ``write_baseline``.
claims.why: The function only builds a dict and returns it; no file I/O is performed in this chunk.

claims.text: Every task is snapshotted (including quarantine ones) so quarantine promotion is still comparable later; only PRIMARY tasks are ever gated (see ``run_gate``).
claims.why: The code snapshots all tasks that have no error and not focus_withheld; it does not distinguish quarantine vs primary. The claim about gating via run_gate is not in this chunk.

claims.text: ERRORED tasks (``run_tier1``) have no recall to snapshot and are skipped here -- they simply get no baseline entry, which makes them a "new task" (not silently a pass) the next time ``run_gate`` sees them resolve successfully.
claims.why: The code filters out tasks with 'error' key (via `if 'error' not in t`).

claims.text: FOCUS-WITHHELD tasks (the secret floor fail-closed on the task's own focus file) are skipped for the same reason: there is no ``recall`` key to snapshot, and re-baselining a fence-refused task would silently launder "never measured" into "passing".
claims.why: The code filters out tasks with `t.get('focus_withheld')`.

claims.text: EXPLICIT-ONLY baseline write. Never call this from an automatic code path -- a baseline that updates itself is not a ratchet, it is a no-op. Only the '--update-baseline' CLI flag (a human decision) should reach this.
claims.why: The docstring describes intended usage policy; the code itself does not enforce any guard against automatic calls.

claims.text: Returns the path written. Deterministic formatting (sorted keys) so the diff is meaningful in review.
claims.why: The chunk ends before the write operation; json.dump with sort_keys is not shown, but it is a typical implementation. Cannot verify from this chunk.
